# morse-runner

**CW contest simulator, the native Lazarus port of VE3NEA's Morse Runner**

- **Version recorded:** 1.68z
- **Categories:** `cw`, `morse-training`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/zmetzing/MorseRunner>

## What it does

Simulates the operator's side of a CW contest pile-up. Stations call you in Morse at the speed you set, with QRM, QRN, QSB, flutter and the occasional lid, and you work them with the function keys -- F1 for CQ, F2 for the exchange, F3 for thanks -- while the program scores what you copied against what was sent. Pile-Up, Single Calls, WPX Competition and HST Competition modes, a recorded score and an optional WAV of the session.

## Why you would want it

Nothing else in this catalog trains contest copying. qrq, xcwcp, ebook2cwgui and wordsworth teach and drill Morse; this is the step after them, copying callsigns out of a crowd at speed. Under AHRL it was a Windows binary under Wine on x86_64 only. This is the same program compiled natively, so there is no Wine.

## Before it will work

A desktop session and working audio. No radio: it generates every signal itself. Set your own callsign in the Station panel first; the default is VE3NEA, the author's.

## How it installs

- git (make) — https://github.com/zmetzing/MorseRunner at `29590a6719c725bc95730e72213a00ef92cfa489` — *on debian, parrot, ubuntu, linuxmint, pop; arch x86_64*
  - build dependencies: `build-essential`, `fpc`, `lcl-utils`, `lcl-units`, `lcl-gtk2`, `libsdl1.2-dev`
  - the project's build system has no install rule; the binaries listed below are copied into the prefix instead
  - Built on 2026-09-30 in a debian:13 rootless Podman container the way this block runs it -- `make -j 2` in the checkout, as an unprivileged user, with exactly the build_depends above -- exit 0, about 10 s and 284 MB peak for lazbuild; the executable is 29.7 MB with debug information and links GTK2 and libSDL-1.2. The build dependencies came to 368 packages and 1.8 GB on a bare debian:13 image, which is why the `morse` profile names this unit rather than including it. The engine's dry run plans it; it has not been installed through the engine on any target, and not built on Parrot, Ubuntu, Mint or arm64.

## What it changes on your machine

- **installed tree** — `/usr/local/share/hammunition/morse-runner` is created and handed to the operator who ran the install by an explicit `chown` step in the plan (**D-043**): the software keeps settings, logs or data beside its executable, so the tree has to be writable by whoever runs it. On a shared machine that means anyone who can act as that user can change what the launcher runs.
  - `/usr/local/share/hammunition` stays root-owned; the tree itself is replaced whole on every install, so anything the software wrote inside it is lost then
  - undo: `hammunition uninstall morse-runner` removes the tree

## Known problems

**This is Morse Runner 1.68 (2006), not the Community Edition.** CE's contests -- CWT, ARRL DX, Field Day, Sweepstakes, CQ WW, NAQP, IARU, the JARL contests, SST -- are in a Windows-only Delphi tree that does not build here (measured 2026-09-30); this port has the original's WPX-style exchange and HST. **Settings are saved beside the executable**, so the installed tree is handed to the operator (D-043) and one account's settings are the machine's. **It prints a debug line for every audio buffer** ("BufferDone ...") to standard output, which a desktop session sends to its log; in the container's unpaced null sink that was hundreds of thousands of lines in a few seconds, and the rate against a real sound card is unmeasured. Audio goes through SDL 1.2, which Debian 13 provides as sdl12-compat over SDL2; playback through PipeWire or a real sound card has not been heard. After a run started under Xvfb the bottom of the window was not redrawn in the screenshot, which may be the virtual display and may not. **Not on Kali** (no GTK2 LCL in its archive) and not yet on arm64.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: rebuild
- The port's last commit is 2022-05-23 and nothing has been tagged. The yearly pin review is for noticing two things: a commit here, or a Linux build in the Community Edition (w7sst/MorseRunner), whose README lists "integrate a recent Linux port" as a goal. The day CE builds natively it supersedes this unit.

## Where to get help with the software itself

Zach Metzinger's port, issues at the URL above; the port's last commit is 2022-05-23, so expect none. The program is Alex Shovkoplyas's (VE3NEA). Licence: the source files carry Mozilla Public License 2.0 headers; the port's tree has no LICENSE file and its Readme still says "freeware" from the 2006 original (read 2026-09-30). The Community Edition, which shares the code, ships MPL-2.0 as LICENSE.md. For contest-simulation questions the Community Edition's project (github.com/w7sst/MorseRunner) is where the Morse Runner community is.
